q: When we go out in public or have people over, I’m embarrassed by his behavior. He got kicked out of a nanny share after only a month because he was too difficult for the nanny to handle.
cx: Mother recovering from a C-section with a newborn and a very physical 2.5-year-old.

q: My husband is hands on in the sense that he is physically present and will take my son to the playground and stuff to get out of the house, but he is always distracted on his phone and he hasn’t made me feel supported in the post partum phase.
cx: Same mother on the partner who is present but not helping.

q: How do I speak to my kid in a way that he will actually listen to? How do I get my husband to get off his phone and pay attention without starting a fight, because I don’t have the energy to get into with him right now?
cx: Her two asks of strangers: words for the child, and words for the husband.

q: However, she has a friend's birthday party in about a week, which is during her naptime, 12:30-3:30 pm. I’m concerned that she’s going to try to withhold her poop during the entire party
cx: Pee trained by day 4 of Oh Crap; poop held for nap diapers; a party coming.

q: I’ve been holding off on naptime until it’s a more reasonable time. I’m hoping to force the issue so she poops on the potty but she’s usually able to hold it for another hour or so.
cx: Delaying the nap diaper to push the poop onto the potty; the child outlasts it.

q: My husband has been telling her that accidents are okay. Which I know is NOT advisable. How do I correct this?
cx: The partner reassures the child; the parent believes the method forbids it.

q: It's starting to make me visibly frustrated - I try to stay calm and let her know she needs to get on the toilet before she starts peeing, but multiple partial accidents a day are starting to drive me insane.
cx: Trained last Thanksgiving; repeated partial-accident regressions since.

q: She supposed to start preschool in the fall and she has to be totally trained, and I feel like I can't send her like this. Do I just power through and see if it resolves again, or do I redo potty training?
cx: The preschool's fully-trained rule as the deadline.

q: I have tried everything from youtube potty training videos, to 15 min sessions in the potty during the day, especially after meals.  I have exhausted every resource.
cx: Months of a 3-year-old holding poop; pee is fine.

q: I tried the rewards technique too but he refuses— for no reason he says "no" to the potty or the toilet.  I think it's a control thing too.
cx: Same parent; rewards already tried.

q: I have tried literally every kind of discipline and nothing works. At all. I am trying so so hard.
cx: Freshly postpartum mother of a nearly-3-year-old in months of tantrums.

q: Send all the advice because I feel like a failure ✨
cx: Same post, the ask.

q: We’ve tried everything we could research. I’ve read probably 15-20 parenting books in the last 4-6 months alone. I’ve tried every parenting method I could find under the sun.
cx: Mother of a defiant 3-year-old who laughs at every consequence.

q: As a matter of fact, he pretty much got kicked out of daycare for repeatedly telling the teacher to shut up to get a reaction and make the other kids laugh. She said if he can’t stop saying it he can’t come back
cx: The in-home daycare's ultimatum.

q: family members of ours have a running “joke” that he will be expelled from preschool his first week, this September coming up.
cx: Relatives' jokes about the child before preschool starts.

q: They’ve even made jokes insinuating that he will be a convict when he’s older, which really hurt a lot.
cx: Same relatives; she says the child is also sweet and loving.

q: I have brought this up to his pediatrician who just shrugged it off as his age and said he will get better at following directions as he gets older.
cx: The paediatrician's answer to her worry.

q: The other day he said to me “mom, I’m scared of you when you’re mad at me”. I felt terrible hearing him say that
cx: Both parents say they can barely hold in their anger after months of patience.

q: I feel like I made the biggest mistake of my life by sending him to daycare.
cx: She believes the mixed-age home daycare taught the swearing and defiance.

q: It is strange to me because at the daycare she goes normally without issues and at home she even announces when its about to happen or when she needs to go.
cx: 16-month-old who used the potty since 6 months now arches and refuses it at home.

q: We bought a different one, we are trying to use different room and are also going to potty "together". All of this helped for about two times.
cx: New potty, new room, sitting together; each worked twice.

q: I tried to look up tips online, but all it said was useless filler text.
cx: Same parent on what online search returned.
